blocks.x: The contract behind Autonomous Supply Chain Control Tower: signed baseline in week two, working slice by week eight, industrialized controls by week twelve, and evidence flowing to your control owner throughout.
The problem this solution exists for
Planning runs on batch snapshots; exceptions consume planners; network re-optimization takes weeks; visibility is stitched from portals.
Our approach

We deliver the control tower: event-driven visibility, demand/inventory/transport decision hubs, agentic exception remediation within policy, scenario engines for disruption, and outcome SLOs that operations leadership steers by.
Reference architecture

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Autonomous Supply Chain Control Tower
blocks.note: Contracts between stages are enforced at the boundary, so schema drift fails loudly in minutes instead of quietly in a quarter.

blocks.x: We engineer Autonomous Supply Chain Control Tower so that regressions are cohorts, not surprises: each stage owns its latency budget and failure policy, and rollback is rehearsed before go-live rather than after the incident.

blocks.x: Platform stack

The solution runs on KYC Management System and EEMS Platform: Many agents operating as one governed, measurable workforce. Enterprise decisions in milliseconds — with a full evidence trail for each decision.
How it runs in an engagement

items: We measure the starting position and lock the baseline with your team — no build work begins before the number is agreed.
A bounded pilot on your real data, with the gate review scheduled before the first commit is written.
Runbooks, enablement and the control trail that let your teams operate it without us in the room.
Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

How a delivery runs

Autonomous Supply Chain Control Tower follows the same delivery pattern as every Achala program — baseline, bounded pilot, gate review, then scale. The difference from a traditional program is that each step produces evidence your auditors can walk.
